warnings: SHOULD-FIX (top; internal AST-carrier + validate_block signature are mutually inconsistent — pin ONE canonical shape before the Coder starts). Three passages describe the block's AST shape THREE different ways: (a) §1.2 says the block is a single `AnnotationArg::Record` whose fields include `version` as a `RecordField`, AND that each `entry` lowers to `Call{"entry",[Record]}`; (b) AT-2900 says the parse output is 'Call{"entry",[Record]} args + block-level version' (i.e. the annotation's top-level `args: Vec<Spanned<AnnotationArg>>` is a MIX of entry-Calls and a version); (c) §1.4 declares `validate_block(block_fields: &[RecordField], span)`. These cannot all be true: a `Call`-wrapped `entry` is an `AnnotationArg`, and `RecordValue` has NO Record/Call variant, so entries CANNOT sit inside a block `Record`'s `fields` NOR be passed as `&[RecordField]`. Either (i) the block is a single `AnnotationArg::Record` and entries are stored as some in-Record shape (contradicts 'entries lower to Call'), or (ii) the top-level annotation args are `[version-carrier, Call{entry,..}, ...]` and `validate_block` must take `&[Spanned<AnnotationArg>]` (splitting version-field(s) from entry-Calls internally) — NOT `&[RecordField]`. Because `AnnotationArg::Record` is a semi-permanent public enum addition explicitly REUSED by the future `@transfer` path (§2.3), pin the exact carrier shape now and correct the `validate_block` parameter type to match the real parse output. This is a Coder-blocking ambiguity, not a grammar-forever hole (the user-facing EBNF §1.3a is unaffected).

SHOULD-FIX (writer-side forward-compat is UNDEFINED — the direction the r1-MF3 probe asked about). §1.4a fully pins the READER's forward-compat (a v1 compiler PRESERVES-AND-WARNS on a version>1 block). But §1.5's writer only says it 'preserves any block-level version/future keys' when splicing — it does NOT define whether `axc log-opt` REFUSES to append into a block whose `version > SUPPORTED_OPT_LOG_VERSION`. A v1 writer can only emit a v1-shaped `entry`; splicing that into a v2 block yields an entry that a FUTURE v2 reader may deem malformed (missing whatever fields v2 made required), and silently mixes schema versions inside one block. Refusing is strictly safer and one line: add `LogOptError::UnsupportedVersion { found, supported }` (source byte-unchanged, exit-coded) when the parsed block's version exceeds SUPPORTED, and an AT. Define it explicitly — 'preserve on read' must not be silently assumed to mean 'append-into on write'.

SHOULD-FIX (contextual-keyword scope inside an entry is under-specified). The EBNF makes `entry`/`version` contextual keywords at BLOCK level (dispatch on the ident string + `{`-vs-`:` lookahead). But `field := ident ":" record_value` means that AS FIELD KEYS INSIDE an entry, `entry`/`version` are ordinary idents → they become unknown-key schema events (v1 REJECT / v>1 PRESERVE-WARN), NOT keyword-parse errors. This is consistent and safe, but state it so the Coder does NOT special-case them inside an entry: `entry { version: 2 }` is an unknown-entry-key reject at v1 (schema), and `entry { entry { .. } }` is a parse error via `field` expecting `:` and seeing `{` (both paths already yield rejection; just name which path so AT-2919's nested-entry fixture asserts the right error variant).

SHOULD-FIX (recovery is NEW code, not inherited from parse_strategy_block). Verified: parse_strategy_block (parser.rs:370-456) returns `None` on the FIRST malformed item (parser.rs:395/401/416/437) — it does NOT recover-and-report-all. §1.2/§1.3a's 'recover at next entry/comma/}' and AT-2913's 'reports ALL bad entries' are therefore genuinely new logic, not a tolerance the strategy path already has. Only the trailing-comma tolerance is analogous. Word the spec so the Coder implements true multi-error recovery (and QA verifies AT-2913 actually surfaces >1 error), rather than copying strategy's bail-on-first-error.
